title: Midazolam — Pediatric Status Epilepticus
sources: Glauser T et al. AES status epilepticus guideline. Epilepsy Curr 2016;16:48-61 (PMID 26900382)
Silbergleit R et al. RAMPART. NEJM 2012;366:591-600
Othman AA et al. Ket-Mid RCT. Pediatr Neurol 2025 (investigational combination)

changelog.change: Added a note on the Ket-Mid RCT (ketamine 2 mg/kg + midazolam 0.2 mg/kg as first-line for pediatric GCSE) — single-centre, 'promising not practice-changing'.

Tier 1 verification: IM 0.2 mg/kg / max 10 mg confirmed (RAMPART: 10 mg ≥ 40 kg, 5 mg for 13-40 kg). IV and intranasal per-dose caps vary by pathway (many cap at 5 mg) — flagged institution-specific; added the RAMPART weight bands.

purpose: First-line benzodiazepine for pediatric status epilepticus when there is no IV access — IM or intranasal.

doses.indication: No IV access — IM or intranasal
doses.notes: IM is at least as effective as IV lorazepam for time-to-seizure-cessation when access has to be established (RAMPART). RAMPART fixed doses: 10 mg for ≥ 40 kg, 5 mg for 13-40 kg. Some peds pathways cap intranasal at 5 mg/dose — confirm locally.
Many pediatric pathways cap IV midazolam at 5 mg/dose; AES 2016 does not list IV midazolam as a first-line agent. Confirm the per-dose cap against your local status-epilepticus pathway.

reversal: Flumazenil is NOT used in the seizure setting (lowers the seizure threshold).
buildNote: Institution-specific caps flagged for reconciliation. Investigational — the Ket-Mid RCT (Othman 2025, single-centre, n=144) gave ketamine 2 mg/kg + midazolam 0.2 mg/kg IV as the FIRST dose for generalized convulsive status epilepticus: 76% vs 21% cessation at 5 min, ~5x fewer intubations, effect largest when the seizure had run > 30 min (synaptic GABA-A internalises / NMDA up-regulates over time). Authors' own framing: 'promising, not practice-changing' — no confirmatory second-site data, ketamine not stocked as a first-line seizure agent in most formularies. Do not change the first-line benzodiazepine recommendation on one trial.
